summary: How this workspace is set up, such as what it calls each level of aim.
definition: How this workspace is set up. It records your vision and mission, which every goal serves, and the words your organisation uses for each level of aim and for a project. It also sets the author name used when no one is signed in, the browser used to make PDFs, and your own examples for fields. There is only one.

/metadata/id.guide: Always default. There is only one settings record.

/spec/purpose.guide: Your vision and mission, and where they are published. If they come from a published plan, copy them word for word and name the section.

/spec/goalLevels.guide: Your organisation's words for the three levels of aim: goal, objective, outcome. Each level keeps its meaning. Leave it empty to keep Goal, Objective and Outcome.

poor.why: Functional names part of an organisation. The third level is what is true once a change is made.
An output is what a project produces; the third level is an outcome, a changed state.

/spec/projectLevelName.guide: Your organisation's word for a project, such as Initiative. It still means work that ends.

poor.why: A programme is a different thing: it coordinates projects and operations towards one change.

/spec/operator.guide: The author name used for changes saved when no one is signed in, such as from the command line. It is local by default. Name the setup or the role that runs it, not a person.

poor.why: A person. Name a role or setup instead.

/spec/chromium.guide: The path to a Chromium browser used to render documents as PDF. Leave it empty to use the CHROMIUM environment variable, or the first Chromium on the path.

/spec/examples.guide: Your own examples for a field, in your organisation's words, up to five per field, keyed by field name such as aim.change, objective or gap.current. Fields without any show the built-in examples.
good: aim.change: Every depot checks produce against one published standard.

poor.why: Leave the number out of the objective. Numbers go in key results.
